- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Apostle Islands are a fantastic destination for kayaking.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested route: Mainland to Oak Island, a 4-6 mile paddle with several campsites and stunning scenery.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested route: Outer Islands Loop, a more challenging route with distances of 8-12 miles and potential wind and wave exposure.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested route: Meyers Beach to Stockton Island, a 4-6 mile paddle with several campsites and scenic beaches.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Campsite options on Oak Island: 11 campsites with picnic tables and latrines, reservations recommended.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Campsite options on Stockton Island: 7 campsites with picnic tables and latrines, reservations recommended.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Campsite options on Raspberry Island: 4 primitive campsites, first-come, first-served.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Campsite options on Devils Island: 2 primitive campsites, first-come, first-served.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for obtaining permits from the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore website before the trip.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Reminder to check the weather forecast before paddling due to changing conditions on Lake Superior.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Caution advised when exploring sea caves, with emphasis on skill level and conditions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Respect for wildlife, including black bears, wolves, and nesting birds, is important.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Follow Leave No Trace principles to minimize impact on the islands' ecosystem.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional resources include the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore website for permits and trip planning.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Kayak rentals and guided tours are available for those not bringing their own gear.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested checking Lake Superior water levels before the trip for planning routes and camping.
